title: Control sprint: Auditor rapid Q&A & evidence transforms
body:
Purpose:
This is a fast-turn, auditor-facing playbook for the upcoming SOC 2 / ISO 27001 walkthroughs focused on RBAC v2, audit-log schema, SIEM export transforms, and evidence automation. The doc is intentionally pragmatic — quick mappings, concrete evidence artifacts, known gaps, and canned Q&A so engineering and security can respond consistently during live auditor sessions.

Scope:
- Controls in-scope: logical access (RBAC), change control and logging, audit log integrity, evidence retention and export, monitoring and alerting tied to SIEM ingestion.
- Components: identity service (idp + internal user-store), RBAC v2 service, API gateway, serving runtime (inference nodes), audit-log pipeline (kafka -> log-transform -> SIEM), evidence automation lambda runbook.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Read the "auditor Q&A" section and script answers verbatim for first 2 rounds of questions.
2) When asked for artifacts, hand over links in the Evidence matrix below (S3 prefixes, snapshot names).
3) If auditor requests live queries, use the prepared SIEM queries under "SIEM quick-queries" and follow the sanitization notes.

Evidence matrix (direct artifacts to provide) — map control -> artifact path / snapshot name / ID:
- Logical access / RBAC enforcement (SOC2 CC6.1 / ISO A.9):
  * artifact: RBAC-v2-role-matrix-2024-10-01.csv (s3://redwood-evidence/rbacv2/role-matrix/role-matrix-2024-10-01.csv)
  * artifact: user-provisioning-log-snapshot-2024-10-01.jsonl (s3://redwood-evidence/provisioning/snapshots/user-provisioning-log-20241001.jsonl)
  * artifact: IAM-OKTA-sync-config (confluence link in linked_artifacts)
- Audit logging and integrity:
  * artifact: audit-log-schema-v2.md (internal spec, contains field definitions)
  * artifact: audit-log-hashchain-proof-2024-10.tgz (hashchain snapshots stored in vault)
  * artifact: siem-export-sample-2024-10.json (s3 sample export)
- Evidence retention / export (ISO/SOC2 retention):
  * artifact: evidence-retention-policy-v1.3.pdf (confluence/KB)
  * artifact: auto-archive-job-manifest-2024-09.yaml (repo path)

Quick gap summary (prioritized):
1) G1 — Missing automated proof-of-integrity for streaming writes older than 90 days. Current state: daily fingerprinting exists but no chain-of-custody metadata passed to SIEM. Impact: auditor wants stronger tamper-evidence. Proposed short-term mitigation: provide hashchain snapshots for prior 6 months and add SIEM field "audit_chain_id" by next sprint. Ticket: SEC-412.
2) G2 — SIEM export strips tenant_id in transformation to anonymize PII; need per-auditor view for multi-tenant evidence. Impact: cannot show tenant-scoped audit trail on demand. Mitigation: retain tenant_id in encrypted column and provide decryption flow under NDA. Ticket: SEC-428.
3) G3 — Few gaps in role-to-resource mapping granularity. Some service roles are grouped; auditors ask for intent mapping. Mitigation: produce an intent matrix doc and add annotations to role-matrix CSV. Ticket: SEC-433.

Log schema (authoritative fields we use internally) — summary (use this when auditor asks for "what's in an audit record?"):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- event_id: uuid v4
- actor_id: user|service id (opaque)
- actor_type: human | service | system
- action: create|read|update|delete|auth|token.issue|token.revoke|config.change|deploy
- resource_type: model|route|deployment|user|key|tenant
- resource_id: opaque id string
- prev_state: brief JSON snapshot (max 2 KB)
- new_state: brief JSON snapshot (max 2 KB)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- request_id: trace id from request path (for cross-service correlation)
- ip_address: ipv4/ipv6 (pseudonymize for exported evidence if required)
- user_agent: client UA
- region: cloud region
- tenant_id: customer id (encrypted in SIEM export)
- retention_bucket: logical label for retention policy
- signer: digital-signature metadata (when available)

SIEM export transforms — producer -> exporter notes (operational checklist):
- Input: JSON lines from kafka topic 'audit-events-v2' (utf-8).
- Transform1: canonicalize timestamp -> RFC3339/ISO8601, drop sub-millisecond noise.
- Transform2: flatten nested resource metadata into resource_* prefix fields (resource_type, resource_id, resource_name).
- Transform3: map action enums to human-readable verbs for the SIEM UI (e.g., token.issue -> "Token issued").
- Transform4: pseudonymize ip_address and actor_id for exported demo bundles unless "auditor_access=true" flag present. Keep mapping in internal secrets manager.
- Transform5: attach audit_chain_id header (from hashchain service) as "audit.chain_id" field. If missing, mark record with "audit.chain_missing": true.
- Output format: newline-delimited JSON, UTF-8, gzip compressed for S3 delivery.

SIEM quick-queries (Splunk / Elasticsearch style examples) — use exactly as-is for live demo:
- "Show all RBAC role changes for tenant X over last 90 days":
  * ES: POST /_search?q=resource_type:role AND tenant_id: "TENANT-1234" AND action:"config.change" AND timestamp:[now-90d TO now]
  * Splunk: index=audit source=audit-events action=config.change tenant_id=TENANT-1234 | stats count by actor_id,resource_id,timestamp
- "Find failed token revocations in last 30 days":
  * ES query: action:token.revoke AND outcome:failure AND timestamp:[now-30d TO now]
  * Splunk: index=audit action=token.revoke outcome=failure | table timestamp,actor_id,resource_id,request_id

Sanitization / NDA rules for exports:
- Never deliver raw logs with plaintext tenant_id or user email outside of encrypted channels.
- If auditor requests tenant-scoped trail, provide an encrypted bundle with a decryption key exchange under NDA and 7-day access window.
- For public demo bundles, replace actor_id and ip_address with stable pseudonyms (pseudonym maps stored in Secrets Manager and not shared).

Evidence automation runbook (how to produce an auditor bundle quickly) — steps:
1) Run snapshot job: aws lambda -> create snapshot of audit-events-v2 for date range X (script: infra/tools/snapshot-audit.sh). Produces s3://redwood-evidence/temp/audit-snapshot-YYYYMMDD.jsonl.gz.
2) Run transform job: infra/transform/siem-export.py --input snapshot --attach-chain --pseudonymize optional_flag. Creates export file in temp bucket.
3) Create integrity proof: run hashchain tool: infra/tools/hashchain-gen --input export.gz -> outputs export.gz.hc (signed).
4) Upload bundle to evidence-bucket with metadata.json that lists tickets and control references.
5) Notify auditor via secure-share link (pre-signed S3 URL with expiration) and update the evidence tracker with artifact ID.

Acceptance criteria for auditor deliverable (what we promise during a walkthrough):
- For RBAC control: provide role-matrix CSV + sample audit records showing enforcement (at least 5 samples per enforcement type: allow/deny/change).
- For logging control: provide schema doc + export sample + hashchain proof for same date window.
- For retention: show policy doc + archive job manifest + evidence file presence in retention bucket.

Scripted auditor Q&A (copy these answers during live session):
Q: How do you prevent unauthorized role changes?
A: Role modifications require an authenticated session, go through the RBAC v2 service where each change is an auditable event. Changes are gated by a change-approval workflow for production-role changes (pull request + CI check + owner approval). The RBAC service enforces the final allow/deny, and every change produces an audit record with request_id and actor_id. We can show the role-matrix and three recent change events.

Q: Can you show proof the logs were not tampered with?
A: Yes — we produce daily hashchain blobs that sign the day’s export using an internal keysafe. For the requested period we will provide the .hc proof bundle; our SIEM exports include the audit.chain_id which ties records to a chain. We will also run a verification script with the auditor if needed.

Q: How do you segregate tenant data in logs for multi-tenant exports?
A: By default we pseudonymize tenant_id in demo exports. For auditor requests we produce an encrypted bundle that retains tenant_id and is delivered under NDA with a 7-day decryption key. We keep an internal mapping in Secrets Manager and log all requests for decryption.

Open questions / decisions needed (for security eng):
- D1: Approve adding "audit_chain_id" to SIEM export (low-risk) — owner: Diego. Target: next sprint.
- D2: Define formal procedure for per-auditor encrypted bundles (who signs the NDA, who approves decryption). Owner: Priya. Target: end of month.
- D3: Confirm retention label renaming in Central KB to match ISO language (retention_bucket -> retention_policy_label). Owner: Liam.

Action items (short-term):
- A1: Create SEC-428 to implement encrypted tenant retention field and decryption flow. (Assignee: Diego)
- A2: Run hashchain backfill for prior 180 days and upload proofs to evidence bucket. (Assignee: infra-runops)
- A3: Prepare 5 sanitized and 3 tenant-scoped sample exports and add to evidence matrix with pre-signed links. (Assignee: security-ops)

Meeting plan with auditor (if live):
- 5 min intro + scope confirmation
- 10 min RBAC walkthrough (role matrix + live query)
- 10 min logging integrity (schema + hashchain proof)
- 10 min SIEM export sample review (transform rules, sanitization)
- 10 min Q&A / on-the-spot evidence pulls

Notes to presenter (do's and don'ts):
- DO have the pre-signed links and sample files open before the call.
- DO not share decrypted tenant bundles over chat; always use S3 pre-signed URL and record the audit.
- DO avoid ad-hoc reconstruction of logs on the call; point to the snapshot and run prepared query instead.
- DON'T speculate about internal keys, just state the hashchain and verification process.

Appendix: Useful quick refs
- RBAC repo PR for role matrix automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/721
- Snapshot script path: infra/tools/snapshot-audit.sh
- Hashchain tool: infra/tools/hashchain-gen
- Evidence bucket prefix: s3://redwood-evidence/

-- End --
